items.title: Runtime pip install into Slicer's shared Python environment (einops==0.6.1)

findings.title: Runtime pip install into Slicer's shared Python environment (einops==0.6.1)
findings.explanation: A search of Easy_fusion found slicer.util.pip_install(requirement) at Easy_fusion.py:2882, and filters.py:65 defines FILTER_EINOPS_REQUIREMENT = "einops==0.6.1". This installs a pinned third-party package into Slicer's shared Python environment, which persists for users and other extensions. I did not read the surrounding lines, so whether the user is explicitly asked first (and whether this can run at import/startup) is unverified; if it runs without confirmation, it violates the index's environment policy.
findings.suggestion: Show an explicit confirmation dialog naming the package and version before installing, never install at import/startup, and avoid an exact pin unless required; document the install in the README.

items.title: Hard pin of einops to an old version

findings.title: Hard pin of einops to an old version
findings.explanation: slicer.util.pip_install installs einops==0.6.1 into Slicer's shared Python environment after user confirmation. An exact pin can conflict with other extensions that need newer einops. Only the user's consent covers this, and the pin is not justified in the code.
findings.suggestion: Use a lower bound such as einops>=0.6.1 unless the model code requires the exact version, and document why.

items.title: MIT license text names a different project ("SlicerPETDenoise")

findings.title: MIT license text names a different project ("SlicerPETDenoise")
findings.evidence: of this software and associated documentation files (the "SlicerPETDenoise"), to deal
findings.explanation: The grant in LICENSE covers 'the "SlicerPETDenoise"' rather than PETReviewCompare, apparently copied from the author's other project. The MIT terms still permit distribution, but the named subject is wrong, which creates ambiguity about what the license covers.
findings.suggestion: Replace the project name with PETReviewCompare (or the actual extension name) in the LICENSE text.

findings.title: LICENSE names a different project
findings.evidence:
Copyright (c) 2025 Burak Demir

Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy
of this software and associated documentation files (the "SlicerPETDenoise"), to deal
findings.explanation: The MIT grant refers to the software as "SlicerPETDenoise", not PETReviewCompare. The grant is still clear for distribution, but the wording should match this extension to avoid ambiguity about what is licensed.
findings.suggestion: Change the parenthetical to the actual project name or remove it.

items.title: PyTorch dependency not declared although AI filters need it

findings.title: PyTorch dependency not declared although AI filters need it
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA") # PyTorch is optional: only the AI post-processing filters need it (installed via the PyTorch extension)
findings.explanation: The AI filters import torch (filters.py:917) and expect the Slicer PyTorch extension to have installed it, but neither EXTENSION_DEPENDS nor the catalog's build_dependencies lists PyTorch/PyTorchUtils. Users who install only this extension get a failure when they try a filter, with no dependency hint in the catalog.
findings.suggestion: Either declare PyTorchUtils in EXTENSION_DEPENDS and build_dependencies, or make the module's error message and README point clearly to the PyTorch extension.

items.title: Sliding-window inference runs on the GUI thread

findings.title: Sliding-window inference runs on the GUI thread
findings.evidence:
with torch.no_grad():
                predictedNoise = sliding_window_inference(
                    inputs=networkInput, roi_size=roiSize, sw_batch_size=1, predictor=predictor,
                    overlap=FILTER_WINDOW_OVERLAP, mode="gaussian", sw_device=device, device=torch.device("cpu"))
findings.explanation: The whole inference runs synchronously in the module's slot; the progress dialog only repaints via slicer.app.processEvents() (filters.py:445). On large volumes this blocks the Slicer UI for minutes and cancellation is only honoured between windows, which can look like a hang.
findings.suggestion: Run the filter in a worker thread (or Slicer CLI) and keep the GUI responsive, or at minimum document the expected duration and keep the cancel check frequent.

findings.title: Test registration commented out
findings.explanation: Both Testing/Python CMakeLists are commented out, so CTest does not run the module tests. The tests in EponaLib/tests.py run only through the in-app self test.
findings.suggestion: Register the unit tests with slicer_add_python_unittest so CI runs them.

items.title: Unbounded module-level cache keyed by node ID

findings.title: Unbounded module-level cache keyed by node ID
findings.explanation: petValueInfo() stores an entry per volume node ID (values.py:413) and never removes entries when nodes are deleted or the scene is closed, so the dict grows for the lifetime of the Slicer session and keeps stale keys.
findings.suggestion: Prune entries for nodes no longer in the scene (e.g. on node-removed events) or use a bounded cache.

items.title: torch.load fallback without weights_only on downloaded model files

findings.title: torch.load fallback without weights_only on downloaded model files
findings.evidence:
state = torch.load(modelPath, map_location=device, weights_only=True)
    except TypeError:  # PyTorch older than 1.13 has no weights_only
        state = torch.load(modelPath, map_location=device)
findings.explanation: Model .pth files are downloaded from GitHub releases (filters.py:38-42) and loaded with torch.load. On PyTorch < 1.13 the code falls back to pickle-based loading without weights_only, so a replaced or tampered release asset would execute arbitrary code at load time. The SHA-256 check (filters.py:577) mitigates this, but when a release asset changes the digest is taken from the same GitHub API, so the trust root is the same.
findings.suggestion: Require torch >= 1.13 (the Slicer PyTorch extension provides newer versions) and remove the unsafe fallback, or refuse to load models without weights_only.

items.title: Large binary assets committed to the repository

findings.title: Large binary assets committed to the repository
findings.explanation: fusbanner.jpg (~3 MB), scr1.jpg (~1.1 MB) and SlicerPETReviewCompare.png (~680 KB) are committed. They are legitimate UI/screenshot resources, but they bloat the repository and every clone; the scan hint flagged the 3 MB banner.
findings.suggestion: Downscale the banner/screenshot or generate them at build time; keep only what the module actually displays.
